static_traits.name: Liu Jing
static_traits.social_status: Has support from one's spouse and friends, but is more reserved in social situations where spicy food is served
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems or psychotherapy history in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, able to describe troubles honestly; good self-awareness, highly cooperative, slightly nervous and shy; overall positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I feel inferiority and self-criticism about my ability to handle spicy food (especially spicy chicken wings); these feelings began a few months ago from a friend's comment on my spice tolerance and have developed into avoiding eating spicy food in front of others.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to come to counseling because this problem has begun to affect my confidence in other areas of life, and I want to resolve it before it escalates further.
growth_experiences: The family of origin and upbringing environment strongly prized the values of 'being strong and tough', linking endurance to personal worth, which makes it easier to take 'whether one is strong enough' as the standard for self-evaluation.

core_beliefs: My value depends on whether I can withstand what others think I 'should be able to withstand' (such as the spiciest food)

special_situations.event: A friend commented on their spice tolerance a few months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot eat very spicy food like others, it means I am not strong enough and will be looked down on
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets higher standards for herself in her heart, demands of herself with 'should'; in front of others avoids exposing the 'weakness' of eating spicy food
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am weak, I am not tough enough

special_situations.event: At Social gatherings with spicy chicken wings or spicy food
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Being unable to eat spicy food in public will bring shame and judgment
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids eating spicy food in front of others, reduces performance in such settings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be able to eat spicy food like everyone, otherwise it is shameful

special_situations.event: When others talk about eating spicy food or when thinking about eating spicy food
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failing to meet the 'can eat spicy' standard equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Drives change through self-criticism and pressuring oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Why can I not do it like others? I am failing

special_situations.event: When trying to gradually increase spiciness but feeling discomfort or being overwhelmed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot adapt to spicier food quickly, it proves I am naturally weak
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stops trying, gives up to avoid failing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves again that I am just a coward/weak person

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by others as a 'strong person', accepted and respected
core_conflict.fear: Fears being seen as weak and being mocked, belittled, and rejected
defense_goal: Avoids exposing 'weakness' through self-criticism and avoiding eating spicy food in front of others
Maintains a sense of control and dignity with high-standard 'should' self-demands

object_relations.self_representation: Oneself, easily looked down on, needing to prove oneself strong
object_relations.object_representation: Others/groups who judge harshly and hold toughness as the standard

object_relations.self_representation: A child/individual who must meet the standard and cannot show weakness
object_relations.object_representation: A caretaker/authority figure emphasizing toughness and endurance
object_relations.linking_affect: Stress, guilt, Fear of being negated

manifestations: Introjecting 'must be strong enough, eat the spiciest' as a rule to follow (using many 'should' self-Demands)
Forcibly binds spicy-food tolerance to self-worth, restricting true preferences and choices
Avoids eating spicy food in public in social settings to avoid being judged
outcomes: Intensified self-criticism and sense of shame
Confidence affected in other areas too

manifestations: Becoming more reserved and Withdrawn in Social situations serving spicy food
Worries about others' evaluations and reduces direct participation in occasions
outcomes: Experiencing the shame of being isolated and unease

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using self-Demands like 'I should be able to eat the spiciest' and 'I must be like others'
Judges oneself by the standard others uphold of 'strong / able to endure'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: When thinking of eating spicy food or when the topic is raised, immediately engages in harsh self-evaluation
Overly restraining oneself and Withdrawing to avoid being seen as weak

positive_force: Has a stable family and friend support system (spouse and friends are generally supportive)
Has a clear motivation to seek help and a positive attitude, willing to try structured behavioral experiments
Work functioning Good, stable sense of role competence (Work not yet affected)
Able to identify and describe negative Automatic thoughts, with some self-awareness
negative_force: Introjecting the rule 'strength = worth', equating spicy-food ability with self-worth
Intense self-criticism and labeling ('I am a coward / weak')
A large number of 'should'-style rigid standards lead to stress and shame
Avoidance behavior in social settings maintains the fear of being judged
Compares with others and worries about negative evaluation, lowering confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids eating spicy food in front of others
antecedent: Social gatherings with spicy chicken wings or spicy food
When the topic is raised or others comment on spice tolerance
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating whether one can eat spicy food with 'whether one is strong', fearing being seen as weak and thereby judged and shamed
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome outcomes (being judged, losing face, shame) to ease present Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Withdrawal from Social situations, reduced interaction; Restricted food choices, further reinforcing Fear of evaluation

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation and self-criticism (such as 'I should be able to do it' and 'I am a coward')
antecedent: Thinking about eating spicy food or others bringing up spicy food
Feeling discomfort or frustration when gradually trying spicier food
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized conditions of worth of 'must be strong' and labeling thinking, generalizing a partial failure into overall 'weakness'
target_behavior.function: Through self-punishment and high-standard self-control, maintains order and face (trying to avoid external evaluation)
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening shame and low self-esteem, Decreased confidence, more giving up and avoidance, maintaining a vicious cycle
